title: Let’s take over the ossified Democratic party and deliver a modern New Deal
text:
Welcome back to How We Win, a Guardian opinion series with leading thinkers, offering bold ideas for America’s political future. Last week, Naomi Klein, Guardian US columnist, argued for taking on the billionaire class. Today’s edition was written by Wajahat Ali, editor of The Left Hook and co-host of The Democracy-ish Podcast.
Change is slow, and then, once in a while, all of a sudden.
In this historic midterm election, the Democrats took control of Congress, won Senate races in traditionally red states including South Carolina, Texas and Kansas, and sent shockwaves through America’s quisling political establishment.
Abdul El-Sayed, Rhodes Scholar and public health official, overcame a wave of Islamophobia, Aipac money, and the turncoat politics of fellow Democrats, such as Haley Stevens, who at the last second emerged as a villainous Bride of John Fetterman. El-Sayed will now be going to Washington DC as the first Muslim US senator.
Most importantly, El-Sayed’s election in the Rust Belt state of Michigan destroyed the establishment myth that progressives aren’t “electable”. It seems that “real Americans” who drink real coffee in real diners, as opposed to us coastal replicants, also want a living wage and to curb billionaires and end aid and fealty to Israel and its ongoing genocide.
The future of America depends on progressive, anti-establishment fighters to champion a politics of transformation, and now, the work begins.
We must strategically take over an ossified, impotent and feckless Democratic party beholden to billionaires and corporate Pac money. Centrist Democratic leaders, such as Chuck Schumer, should wait to celebrate. This election was a repudiation of failed Republican policies, but it doesn’t guarantee a political realignment. The aggrieved majority is desperately hungry for real change.
 The future of America depends on progressive, anti-establishment fighters to champion a politics of transformation.
For the past decade, Americans have continued to reject the status quo. There’s a reason why Donald Trump, huckster, unqualified fraudster and accused rapist, became the president of the United States, and that democratic socialists, such as AOC, Bernie Sanders and Zohran Mamdani, are the most popular Democratic elected officials.
The Democratic party’s donors and leaders have shown that their big tent only opens to the right, and that they will continue to punch anyone to their left. They would rather make love to Liz Cheney, Never Trump Republicans, and mythical, white centrist voters than their own base, which includes pro-Palestinian activists, democratic socialists and progressive streamers like Hasan Piker.
The future and success of the progressive movement in the US start at the grassroots and with a populist, anti-establishment message. The progressive movement must create a multicultural majority against fascists and billionaires by repeating a “top v bottom” story, pitting the elite versus the masses.
The villains aren’t transgender athletes or pro-Palestinian activists and student protesters. They aren’t the ones stealing your data, polluting your land with AI datacenters, starting illegal wars, making millions off of corporate mergers or gaining permanent tax cuts at the expense of your Medicaid. The villains are the 1%, also known as the Epstein class and the techno-bros, who dole out money to both sides of the political aisle.
From here on out, it must be “affordability and accountability for all”. No one will be sacrificed to placate bad-faith rightwing rage and propaganda. As we’ve seen over the past two years, fascists start with the most marginalized, such as transgender people and the undocumented, but eventually come for everyone, even their own. (Enjoy your retirement, Senators Thom Tillis and John Cornyn.)
Instead, we respond with a better story. We build upon local community organizing that has emerged to protect immigrants from ICE raids and remove Flock cameras and AI datacenters across the US. When mobilized, these groups multiply into mass peaceful protests, such as the No Kings Rallies, or successful boycotts of companies, such as Target, Disney+ and Spotify. Workers must continue to be protected and supported as unionization efforts grow in the face of severe corporate backlash from companies such as Amazon and Starbucks, which spare no expense to crush collective action.
However, without political power, we cannot achieve widespread reform.
Until progressives capture the Democratic party and its political machinery, they must make do with a systematic culling, winning local and state elections across the country. Currently, the Working Family party is an excellent vehicle that recruits and trains “people-powered candidates” to win elections, mostly as Democrats and Independents. Their candidates include AOC, Mamdani and Brad Lander in New York; Melat Kiros in Colorado, Chris Rabb in Philadelphia, Deb Haaland in New Mexico and Angie Nixon, who would have won the senate race in Florida had the Democratic party chosen to invest in her.
Nixon’s campaign demonstrates the power of grassroots, peer-to-peer, community organizing that actually connects with people and inspires them to come out and vote. It also offers a workable litmus test for progressive candidates who are promising change. Progressives must draw a line in the sand on specific issues to ensure they fulfill their promise to help families struggling with healthcare debt, high gas prices and stagnant wages. They have to make the case with passionate conviction to inspire the masses, who are increasingly coming on board.
These should be our top 10 priorities:
- Tax billionaires.
- Medicare for All.
- Abolish ICE and put forth an immigration reform policy that centers both humanity and security.
- Call out Israel’s genocide and withhold money and weapons from foreign countries that commit war crimes with our resources.
- A living wage.
- Reject corporate Pac money and deliver campaign finance reform.
- Combat climate change and move away from fossil fuels.
- Expand and aggressively reform the supreme court, because without that, we get nothing.
- Deliver accountability for “the Epstein class”, a transnational syndicate of powerful billionaires who commit crimes with impunity.
- Never sacrifice or abandon any marginalized group in our pursuit of affordability and accountability.
Ultimately, progressives must strike fast and hard with Teddy Roosevelt’s “big” antitrust stick to weaken monopolies and deliver a modern FDR “New Deal” to help American workers. Unfortunately, time is not on our side. We must stave off white nationalist, “populist” candidates from the right and the corporate-funded centrists from the Democratic establishment. Unlike Marie Antoinette, Elon Musk and Peter Thiel won’t even leave us cake.
Fascism is not inevitable. Just look at the election results. We can defeat the broligarchy. But it will take a thousand small cuts instead of a single haymaker. Progress takes time and collective work. We, the people, can still have nice things. We deserve it. The story is still being written. We can still have our inshallah. We just have to fight for it.
